verses.text: And I turned and lifted my eyes and saw, and look, a scroll flying.
verses.strongs_text: And I turned{H7725} and lifted{H5375} my eyes{H5869} and saw{H7200}, and look{H2009}, a scroll{H4039} flying{H5774}.
work: הנה: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. In a vision narrative where something suddenly appears, H2009 'lo!' fits as the exclamation introducing the scroll.
מגלה: H4039 'a roll/scroll' vs H4040 (Aramaic equivalent). H4039 is the Hebrew form and fits this Hebrew text.

verses.text: And he said to me, What are you seeing? And I said, I am seeing a scroll flying, its length twenty by the cubit and its width ten by the cubit.
verses.strongs_text: And he said{H559} to{H413} me, What{H4100} [are] you{H859} seeing{H7200}? And I said{H559}, I{H589} [am] seeing{H7200} a scroll{H4039} flying{H5774}, its length{H753} twenty{H6242} by the cubit{H520} and its width{H7341} ten{H6235} by the cubit{H520}.
work: אל/י: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. With a first-person suffix and following speech, H413 'to me' is the natural directional preposition.
אתה: H857 'to arrive', H859 'you (2ms)'. The morph hint says 2ms pronoun and the context is a question addressed to the prophet; H859 'you' fits.
ראה (first): H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7203 'seer/vision'. Morphology is participle masculine singular; in context of 'What are you seeing?', H7200 as participle 'seeing' fits.
אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'ship/fleet'. The prophet is responding to a question; H589 'I' is the obvious choice.
ראה (second): Same as above; H7200 participle 'seeing'.
מגלה: H4039 'scroll/roll' — same as verse 1.
ב/אמה (both): H519 'maidservant', H520 'cubit', H521 (Aramaic cubit), H523 'nation'. In context of measuring dimensions (twenty... ten...), H520 'cubit' is the clear choice.
רחב: H7337 'to broaden', H7338 'a width', H7339 'avenue', H7341 'width', H7342 'roomy'. With possessive suffix and parallel to 'length', H7341 'width' is the correct nominal form.
עשר: H6235 'ten', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth'. Following the dimension pattern (twenty cubits length, __ cubits width), H6235 'ten' is clearly correct.

verses.text: And he said to me, This is the curse going out over the face of all the land, for every one who steals from this [side] according to it has been cleansed, and every one who swears from this [side] according to it has been cleansed.
verses.strongs_text: And he said{H559} to{H413} me, This{H2063} [is] the curse{H423} going out{H3318} over{H5921} the face{H6440} of all{H3605} the land{H776}, for{H3588} every{H3605} one who steals{H1589} from this{H2088} [side] according to{H3644} it has been cleansed{H5352}, and every{H3605} one who swears{H7650} from this{H2088} [side] according to{H3644} it has been cleansed{H5352}.
work: ה/אלה: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'an imprecation/curse', H424 'oak', H426 'God (Aramaic)', H428 'these/those'. With the article prefix and as predicate noun ('this is the ___'), H423 'curse' fits the context of a flying scroll bearing judgment over the land.
על: H5920 'the top/Most High', H5921 'over/upon', H5923 'yoke'. Governing 'the face of all the land', H5921 'over' is the spatial preposition needed.
כל (all instances): H3605 'the whole/every' vs H3606 (Aramaic). Hebrew text uses H3605.
ה/גנב: H1589 'to thieve' vs H1590 'a thief'. With the article and participle morphology ('the one stealing'), H1589 as participle form fits.
מ/זה (both): H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. With preposition מ meaning 'from', H2088 'this' makes sense as 'from this [side]'.
כמו/ה (both): H3644 'as/according to' with 3fs suffix, meaning 'according to it' — referring back to the scroll/curse.

נקה (both): H5352 'to be clean/acquit/cut off'. The Niphal (passive) form means 'has been cleaned out' or 'purged/cut off'. The verb carries both senses of acquittal and extirpation; in the context of a curse against thieves and false swearers, the 'cut off/purged' sense applies.
notes: The verb נקה in Niphal carries an ambiguity: it can mean 'acquitted/held innocent' or 'cut off/extirpated'. The curse context strongly favors the destructive sense — those who steal or swear falsely will be purged out.

verses.text: I have brought it out, declares YHWH of hosts, and it has come to the house of the thief and to the house of the one who swears by my name falsely, and it has lodged in the midst of his house and consumed it and its timbers and its stones.
verses.strongs_text: I have brought it out{H3318}, declares{H5002} YHWH{H3068} of hosts{H6635}, and it has come{H935} to{H413} the house{H1004} of the thief{H1590} and to{H413} the house{H1004} of the one who swears{H7650} by my name{H8034} falsely{H8267}, and it has lodged{H3885} in the midst{H8432} of his house{H1004} and consumed{H3615} it and its timbers{H6086} and its stones{H68}.
work: נאם: H5001 'to whisper/utter as oracle' vs H5002 'an oracle/declaration'. As a construct noun ('declaration of YHWH'), H5002 fits.

ו/באה: The candidate listed is H872 'an entrance', but the traditional ID is H935 'to come/enter'. The verb באה as Qal perfect 3fs of בוא (H935) makes contextual sense — the curse 'has come/entered' the house.
אל (both): H413 'to/toward' — directional preposition governing 'the house of'.
ה/גנב: H1589 'to thieve' vs H1590 'a thief'. Here the morphology is noun ('the thief'), so H1590 fits.
ל/שקר: H8265 'to ogle', H8266 'to be untrue', H8267 'an untruth/falsehood'. With the preposition ל and as adverbial modifier of swearing, H8267 'falsely/falsehood' fits.
בית (all instances): H1004 'house' — the standard Hebrew form.
את (both instances): H853 definite object marker — introducing the objects 'its timbers' and 'its stones'.

verses.text: And the messenger who was speaking with me went out and said to me, Lift now your eyes and see what this is going out.
verses.strongs_text: And the messenger{H4397} who was speaking{H1696} with me went out{H3318} and said{H559} to{H413} me, Lift{H5375} now{H4994} your eyes{H5869} and see{H7200} what{H4100} this{H2063} [is] going out{H3318}.
work: ה/מלאך: H4397 'messenger/angel' vs H4398 (Aramaic). Hebrew form H4397.
ה/דבר: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Participle with article ('the one speaking'), H1696 fits.
נא: H4994 'now/I pray' vs H4995 'raw' vs H4996 'No (Thebes)'. As a particle of entreaty attached to the imperative 'lift', H4994 is correct.
ראה: H7200 'to see' — imperative form here.
ה/זאת: H2063 'this' — feminine demonstrative referring to the thing going out.

verses.text: And I said, What is it? And he said, This is the ephah going out. And he said, This is their appearance in all the land.
verses.strongs_text: And I said{H559}, What{H4100} is it{H1931}? And he said{H559}, This{H2063} [is] the ephah{H374} going out{H3318}. And he said{H559}, This{H2063} [is] their eye{H5869} in all{H3605} the land{H776}.
work: ה/איפה: H374 'ephah (a measure)' vs H375 'what place?/where?'. The article ה- plus the context of identifying a visible object favors H374 'ephah' — a measuring container.

עינ/ם: The consonants עינ with 3mp suffix. H5869 'eye/appearance'. With the possessive 'their', this likely means 'their eye/appearance' — i.e., the visible likeness or aspect of the people throughout the land.
notes: The phrase 'this is their eye in all the land' is striking. The word עין can mean 'eye' or 'appearance/aspect'. The sense seems to be that the ephah represents the visible character or appearance of the people across the land.

verses.text: And look, a disc of lead was lifted up, and this was one woman sitting in the midst of the ephah.
verses.strongs_text: And look{H2009}, a disc{H3603} of lead{H5777} [was] lifted up{H5375}, and this{H2063} [was] one{H259} woman{H802} sitting{H3427} in the midst{H8432} of the ephah{H374}.
work: הנה: H2009 'lo!/behold' — introducing the next element of the vision.
ככר: H3603 'a circle/disc/talent/loaf' vs H3604 (Aramaic). In context of a lead object serving as a lid, H3603 as 'disc/talent' (a round, weighty object) fits.
נשאת: H5379 'something lifted/carried' — passive participle feminine, describing the lead disc being lifted up to reveal what is inside.

אשה: H800 'fire', H801 'burnt offering', H802 'woman'. The subject is described as 'one' (feminine) 'sitting in the midst of the ephah' — H802 'woman' produces a coherent image of a figure seated inside the container.
ה/איפה: H374 'ephah' — same as verse 6.

verses.text: And he said, This is wickedness. And he threw her into the midst of the ephah, and he threw the stone of lead onto its mouth.
verses.strongs_text: And he said{H559}, This{H2063} [is] wickedness{H7564}. And he threw{H7993} her{H853} into{H413} the midst{H8432} of the ephah{H374}, and he threw{H7993} the stone{H68} of lead{H5777} onto{H413} its mouth{H6310}.
work: ה/רשעה: H7564 'wickedness/wrong' — with the article, 'the wickedness'.
את/ה: H853 object marker with 3fs suffix — 'her'.
אל (first): H413 'into' — direction of the throwing.
ה/איפה: H374 'ephah'.
אבן: H68 'stone' vs H69 (Aramaic) vs H70 'potter's wheel/stool'. In construct with 'lead', H68 'stone' makes sense as a weighty object — a stone/weight of lead.
אל (second): H413 'onto/toward' — the lead weight is thrown onto the mouth of the ephah.

verses.text: And I lifted my eyes and saw, and look, two women coming out, and wind was in their wings, and they had wings like the wings of the stork, and they lifted the ephah between the earth and the sky.
verses.strongs_text: And I lifted{H5375} my eyes{H5869} and saw{H7200}, and look{H2009}, two{H8147} women{H802} coming out{H3318}, and wind{H7307} [was] in their wings{H3671}, and they{H2007} had wings{H3671} like the wings{H3671} of the stork{H2624}, and they lifted{H5375} the ephah{H374} between{H996} the earth{H776} and between{H996} the sky{H8064}.
work: ו/ארא: The candidates list only H690 'Ara (a name)', but the traditional ID is H7200 'to see'. The consonants ארא with waw-consecutive match a 1cs form of ראה; this is a common spelling variation. Choosing H7200 'and I saw'.
הנה: H2009 'lo!/behold' — introducing the vision element.
רוח: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/space', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit'. With the preposition 'in their wings', H7307 'wind' produces the image of wind filling their wings — enabling flight.
ו/ל/הנה: H2007 'them/they' vs H2009 'behold'. With the preposition ל and 3fp suffix, H2007 'to them/they had' fits — describing what belonged to these women.
ה/חסידה: H2624 'stork' — the maternal/kind bird with large wings, providing the simile for the women's wings.
בין... ו/בין: H996 'between' — used twice to form 'between X and Y'.
ה/איפה: H374 'ephah'.

verses.text: And I said to the messenger who was speaking with me, Where are they carrying the ephah?
verses.strongs_text: And I said{H559} to{H413} the messenger{H4397} who was speaking{H1696} with me, Where{H575} [are] they{H1992} carrying{H3212} the ephah{H374}?
work: אל: H413 'to' — directional preposition toward the messenger.
ה/מלאך: H4397 'messenger/angel'.
ה/דבר: H1696 'to speak' — participle 'the one speaking'.

אנה: The candidates show H578 'to groan' and H579 'to approach/meet'. However, the traditional ID is H575 (not listed in candidates) meaning 'where?/whither?'. The consonants אנה support an interrogative adverb 'where/whither'. In context of asking about the destination of the ephah, 'where?' is the only reading that makes sense.

המה: The candidate listed is H1993 'to make a loud sound/rage'. However, the traditional ID is H1992 'they' (3mp pronoun). The consonants המה can be the pronoun 'they'. In context ('where are they carrying'), the pronoun H1992 fits.
ה/איפה: H374 'ephah'.

verses.text: And he said to me, To build for it a house in the land of Shinar, and [when] it is established, it will be set there on its base.
verses.strongs_text: And he said{H559} to{H413} me, To build{H1129} for it a house{H1004} in the land{H776} of Shinar{H8152}, and [when] it is established{H3559}, it will be set{H3240} there{H8033} on{H5921} its base{H4369}.
work: אל/י: H413 'to me'.
בית: H1004 'house'.
שנער: H8152 'Shinar' — the plain in Babylonia.
שם: H8033 'there' vs H8034 'name' vs H8035 'Shem'. As an adverb of place following the verbs of establishing and setting, H8033 'there' is correct.
על: H5921 'upon/on' — governing 'its base'.
מכנת/ה: H4369 'a base/pedestal' with 3fs suffix — 'its base'. This refers to the permanent resting place prepared for the ephah.

section_notes: This passage (Zechariah 5:1-11) presents two interconnected visions: the flying scroll (vv. 1-4) and the woman in the ephah (vv. 5-11). The scroll carries a curse against thieves and false swearers; the ephah contains 'Wickedness' personified as a woman, who is carried to Shinar (Babylon) for permanent installation.

The word איפה (ephah) appears repeatedly and was consistently chosen as H374 (a dry measure/container) rather than H375 ('where?') because it always carries the article and functions as a concrete noun in the vision.

The consonants ארא in verse 9 present a difficulty: the only dictionary candidate listed is H690 (a proper name 'Ara'), but the context clearly requires H7200 'to see'. This is a well-known orthographic variation of the 1cs imperfect of ראה.

The verb נקה in verse 3 (Niphal) carries a dual semantic range — both 'acquitted/cleansed' and 'cut off/purged'. The curse context indicates the destructive sense: those who transgress will be purged from the community.
